summary: H.O.M.E. (Habitat of Our Missing Endangered) is a web-based environmental education and monitoring platform that focuses on the impact of forest and land fires on the habitats and survival of wildlife in Indonesia. The platform integrates an "Indonesia Fire & Smoke Monitoring Map" with a "Wildlife Rescue Mission Game," linking environmental data with an interactive learning experience. Through its mapping feature, H.O.M.E. provides visualizations of hotspots and the spread of smoke from fires across various regions in Indonesia, allowing users to understand the fire situation and the potential threats posed to surrounding ecosystems. Meanwhile, the "Wildlife Rescue Mission Game" offers a simulation of search-and-rescue missions for wildlife whose habitats are threatened by fires, while simultaneously providing information about different animal species, their habitats, and the challenges they face in order to survive. The system is designed to transform technical environmental data into a digital experience that is more accessible, engaging, and interactive for the general public, students, and environmentally conscious communities. Ultimately, H.O.M.E. aims to raise public awareness regarding the threats posed by forest and land fires, highlight the importance of protecting wildlife habitats, and foster a commitment to preserving Indonesia’s biodiversity through the use of mapping technology and gamification.
details:
WHAT H.O.M.E DOES

H.O.M.E. is an end-to-end environmental intelligence and forest fire mitigation platform in Indonesia. It automatically integrates remote sensing data—utilizing satellite-based SAR/NISAR radar—to generate fire risk reports, analyze ecological impacts, and calculate environmental compliance indices for government agencies and corporations. Operators and conservation organizations can monitor the spread of smoke from forest fires in real-time, even through thick haze, allowing for immediate assessment of the risk of habitat destruction. The platform also incorporates a rescue-mission game featuring endemic wildlife, which transforms environmental emergency data into interactive missions for the public to help secure affected animals within their natural habitats.

THE IMPACT WE AIM TO ADDRESS


SDG 15: Life on Land

"Behind walls of impenetrable smoke, terrified orangutans cling helplessly to burning branches—our radar pierces through the darkness to find them before their only home becomes their unmarked grave."

SDG 13: Climate Action

"In a few desperate hours, millennia of ancient peat that kept our planet cool bleed into the atmosphere as suffocating ash, quietly stealing tomorrow from generations who haven't even had the chance to live."



SDG 3: Good Health and Well-being

"Hundreds of miles away across the sea, innocent children wake up coughing behind sealed bedroom windows, breathing the poisoned ghosts of a burning forest they were born too late to save."

HOW IT WORKS

1) Integration of Forest and Land Fire Data and Wildlife Habitats 

H.O.M.E. (Habitat of Our Missing Endangered) integrates multi-source Earth observation and biodiversity datasets to connect active forest and land fires (Karhutla) with threatened wildlife habitats across Indonesia: 

  • Active Fire & Thermal Data: Uses NASA FIRMS public Near Real-Time (NRT) feeds—VIIRS 375m (Suomi-NPP & NOAA-20) and MODIS 1km (Terra/Aqua)—alongside NASA GIBS thermal anomaly map tiles to obtain hotspot coordinates, detection timestamps, and Fire Radiative Power (FRP).
  • SAR Radar & Burned Area Data: Incorporates ESA Sentinel-1 (C-Band) and NASA-ISRO NISAR (L-Band) Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) backscatter concepts alongside MODIS MCD64A1 historical burned-area data to penetrate dense wildfire smoke haze and monitor subsurface peatland drying and burn scars.
  • Wildlife Habitat & Conservation Data: Combines IUCN Red List conservation statuses (focusing on Critically Endangered and Endangered endemic species), GBIF wildlife occurrence records, and WDPA (World Database on Protected Areas) boundaries.
  • Spatial Harmonization & Geocoding: All heterogeneous feeds (CSV, JSON, GeoJSON, and map tiles) are normalized into unified schemas and reverse-geocoded to Indonesian Regencies/Cities, Provinces, and Peatland Hydrological Units (Kesatuan Hidrologis Gambut / KHG) so they operate seamlessly within a single geospatial platform.

2) Spatial Analysis of Threats to Habitats 

We develop a spatial analysis approach to connect hotspots and smoke distribution with wildlife habitat areas. 

This analysis can use three main indicators: 

  • AAA (Fire Proximity & Intensity): Proximity of detected NASA FIRMS hotspots to wildlife habitat corridors combined with Fire Radiative Power (FRP).
  • SSS (Smoke Exposure & SAR Signal): Haze obstruction and subsurface peatland drying / surface drop indicators derived from Optical EO vs. SAR radar backscatter (dB).
  • HHH (Habitat Sensitivity): Ecological sensitivity based on peatland/forest ecosystem type, protected-area status (WDPA), and the presence of IUCN CR/EN endemic species.

These indicators form the conceptual Habitat Threat Indicator (HTI), an educational index illustrating potential pressure on wildlife habitats:

HTI=wAA+wSS+wHH

Where AAA, SSS, and HHH represent the normalized indicators above, and wAw_AwA​, wSw_SwS​, wHw_HwH​ are their respective weights.
Note: Weight calibration and normalization require ongoing ecological validation; HTI is designed as an educational risk indicator and should not be interpreted as a statistical fire-ignition probability or direct proof of wildlife casualties.

3) Wildlife Mission Recommendation Algorithm 

To bridge satellite monitoring with interactive learning, H.O.M.E. connects real map regions directly to playable rescue scenarios.

How it works: 

  1. The user inspects fire-affected regencies, SAR radar swaths, and endemic wildlife corridors on the interactive Indonesia Fire & Wildlife Map.
  2. The system identifies the region's dominant peatland/forest biome and threatened species at risk (e.g., Bornean Orangutan, Sumatran Tiger, Helmeted Hornbill, Sun Bear, or Sunda Pangolin).
  3. Selecting a hotspot or wildlife corridor recommends and pre-configures a matching rescue mission in the Rescue Missions Hub, passing the selected target species into the mission briefing.

Through this workflow, abstract satellite coordinates on a map are transformed into a tangible, species-focused conservation experience.

 

4) Gamification and Learning Evaluation System 

The Wildlife Rescue Missions Hub translates Earth observation and peatland firefighting concepts into two playable arcade experiences:

  • SAR Radar Rescue: Players sweep through thick wildfire smoke using simulated Sentinel-1/NISAR SAR radar pulses across 3 forest biomes to locate and extract trapped endemic wildlife before time runs out while avoiding active hotspots.
  • Water-Bomb Arcade: Classic grid-based arcade action across 5 progressively harder stages, where players drop water bombs, clear burning peat obstacles, collect power-ups, stop Oil-Canister Forest Arsonists and Blue Oil-Fire threats, and rescue trapped animals.

5) Environmental Dashboard 

All monitoring, analysis, and gamified modules converge in the H.O.M.E. Platform, enabling users to explore: 

  • Interactive Satellite & SAR Map: Optical EO vs. Radar SAR view modes, historical Before/Now fire comparison, active FIRMS hotspots, and IUCN CR/EN wildlife corridors.
  • Field Dossier & Threat Indicators: Regional summaries of fire temperature, FRP, SAR backscatter (dB), peat moisture/NDVI drop, and affected endemic species.
  • Gamified Rescue Missions & Storytelling: Interactive conservation narratives and playable rescue missions.
  • Verified Conservation Partner Routing: Transparent links directing users who wish to take real-world action to verified non-profit conservation partners (BOS Foundation and Yayasan IAR Indonesia / YIARI), with an explicit disclaimer that H.O.M.E. does not process donations directly.

Thus, H.O.M.E. functions not only as a monitoring tool but also as an environmental education platform that connects data, mapping technology, and gamification. 

6) Business Model Integration

The sustainability of a technological innovation for environmental conservation is measured not merely by the accuracy of its satellite data or the appeal of its gamified missions, but by the platform’s ability to foster a self-sustaining economic ecosystem. Through our "H.O.M.E." business model integration strategy, we have designed a sustainable commercialization framework that bridges institutional environmental regulatory compliance, strategic partnerships within the land insurance sector, and active public participation thereby generating tangible ecological impact while ensuring healthy, recurring year-over-year SaaS revenue growth. 

BENEFITS AND GOALS

H.O.M.E. provides immediate added value by accelerating the monitoring of smoke dispersion from forest and land fires, enhancing compliance with environmental regulations, and mitigating the risk of fire-related losses. Utilizing an interactive map based on NISAR/SAR satellite radar, the system empowers operators and government authorities to detect hotspots even through thick smoke in real time, enabling proactive intervention. In the long term, our system aims to curb habitat destruction caused by forest and land fires, transform engagement in wildlife-rescue-themed games into tangible economic support for conservation, and assist insurance companies and the government in establishing more equitable forest protection policies. This platform serves as a stepping stone toward active ecosystem restoration and the rehabilitation of habitats for Indonesia’s endemic wildlife. 

A conventional balance sheet only knows how to measure what human hands can exploit—timber logged, palm oil harvested, and dividends cashed. But deep inside the suffocating haze of Kalimantan’s peatlands, the true cost of destruction is written in a currency that ordinary ledgers choose to ignore. The Rp 18.5 Billion in projected losses averted by 2028 is not an abstract corporate metric; it is the economic shadow of a living sanctuary reduced to silent, smoldering ash. Every digit in that projection represents an ancient ironwood canopy that took centuries to grow, the sacred carbon of our ancestors burned into toxic vapor, and a terrified mother orangutan clutching her whimpering infant tight against her chest with nowhere left to climb as the fire devours the only home they have ever known.

Every dry season, hundreds of billions of rupiah are poured into emergency water-bombing flights, but dropping water from the sky onto deep subterranean peat is merely an expensive monument to human regret—a desperate shower over an already blackened graveyard. By the time ordinary satellites detect the smoke, the underground fires have already incinerated the roots of the forest, leaving rescue teams to wander blindly through the fog only to find charred remains. The platform investment outlined here—from the initial Rp 2.3 Billion deployment to its scaled radar infrastructure—is not a mere line item of software costs. It is an act of mercy through technology: a synthetic aperture radar that pierces through blinding smog in the fire's very first hours, finding the fragile spark before it turns into an inferno and extinguishing the blaze before innocent lives are suffocated in the dark.

When this calculation reveals a Net Value Preserved of Rp 9.9 Billion and a Return on Prevention of 2.15x, it proves that safeguarding our earth’s final wilderness is the only investment that pays dividends in life itself. That preserved wealth does not sit in a corporate bank account; it lives in the sacred peat that continues to keep our boiling atmosphere cool. It breathes in the fragile lungs of young children hundreds of miles across the sea, who will not have to wake up coughing blood behind taped bedroom windows. And above all, it lives in the quiet heartbeat of an endangered creature who will open her eyes tomorrow morning beneath a lush, green canopy, completely unaware that behind these numbers, a choice was made to save her life before it was too late.


RECOMENDATION & VISION

How our platform addresses immediate environmental compliance and long-term ecosystem sustainability: 

  • Universal ESG & Forestry Compliance: Facilitate the submission of Ecosystem & Wildlife Mitigation Plans (EWMP) and mandatory ISPO/ESG compliance audits for all land concessions and plantations in high-risk areas. Our platform automates these reporting processes, reducing administrative burdens for smallholder operators and cooperatives while ensuring national standardization. 
  • Continuous H.O.M.E. Monitoring: Provide an interactive, real-time spatial dashboard—updated regularly via SAR/NISAR satellite radar—that enables government authorities, disaster management agencies (BPBD), and conservation organizations to track hotspots (even through thick haze) and assess risks to habitats, facilitating timely evacuation and mitigation efforts. 
  • Active Habitat Restoration and Wildlife Corridor Development: Outline your Phase 2 vision—deploying field patrol units and targeted reforestation programs to restore degraded forest areas and establish safe corridors for endemic wildlife. Emphasize that this represents both a green business partnership opportunity and a vital necessity for biodiversity conservation. 
  • High-Efficiency Monitoring Mission Design: Leverage integrated spatial analytical models to advise land managers and spatial planners on optimal protection zones (e.g., defining critical restoration radii), ensuring rapid ecosystem recovery with minimal resource allocation. 
  • Open Conservation Data Sharing: Advocate for a national and international environmental data-sharing framework in collaboration with the Ministry of Environment and Forestry (KLHK), the Meteorology, Climatology, and Geophysics Agency (BMKG), and global research institutions allowing stakeholders to contribute data on hotspots, radar imagery, and wildlife population distribution. This will strengthen machine learning models and enhance the accuracy of ecological risk assessments.
